title: Balance Sheet Audit Trail
summary: Upload a workbook with SOFP, Trial Balance and General Ledger sheets and get a line-by-line audit trail showing how each Statement of Financial Position figure ties back to its supporting TB accounts and GL transactions, with unmapped accounts flagged for you to assign.
assumptions: The SOFP sheet has a row of year headers and uses the most recent year's column as the reported closing balance
The TB sheet has Debit/Credit columns (or a single Closing Balance column); when several Debit/Credit pairs exist, the one labelled End/Closing is used
The GL sheet has one block per account: an account-name row, an optional Initial Balance row, then Date/Debit/Credit/Balance transaction rows
Automatic TB-to-SOFP-line and GL-to-TB-account matching is a starting suggestion based on name similarity and common accounting terms, not guaranteed to be fully correct
Nothing is persisted to disk; uploaded workbooks and reconciliation state live only in server memory for the running process
gaps: Note-linked disclosures (separate note sheets referenced by a Note column on the SOFP) are not cross-referenced automatically
Sign-convention mismatches are flagged, not auto-corrected, since the correct convention can't be inferred reliably from the data alone
expects: An Excel workbook (.xlsx or .xlsm) containing a Statement of Financial Position (SOFP) sheet, a Trial Balance (TB) sheet, and a General Ledger (GL) sheet with one transaction block per account

history.prompt: Create a generic Balance Sheet Audit Support feature that accepts an uploaded Excel workbook (following the same structure as the provided sample workbook) as input. The workbook will contain at least three sheets: "SOFP", "TB New 2025", and "GL New 2025" (or equivalent configurable sheet names). The feature should automatically read the workbook, identify the Statement of Financial Position (SOFP), Trial Balance (TB), and General Ledger (GL) data, and generate an end-to-end audit trail for every Balance Sheet head. For each SOFP closing balance, identify the relevant TB and GL account(s), derive the closing balance from the underlying GL data, present a detailed breakup showing how the reported balance is composed, reconcile the aggregated GL balance with the reported SOFP balance, and clearly flag any differences, missing mappings, or unreconciled amounts. The output should be a structured audit report that enables Finance and Audit teams to trace every reported Balance Sheet figure back to its supporting ledger accounts and transactions without manually reviewing the entire General Ledger. The implementation should work for any uploaded workbook that follows the same tabular structure as the sample, rather than being hardcoded to a specific file.
